column1: # Sanskrit vowel length — DERIVED, do not edit.
# Produced by tools/gen-vowel-length.py from the pinned UCD. The long
# vowel's Unicode NAME is the short one's with its final letter doubled,
# which is why ऋ/ॠ and ऌ/ॡ are found even though their code points are
# not adjacent — an arithmetic rule would get three of five pairs right.
# Pāṇini's table has nine vowels because a sūtra's `अ` means अ and आ
# alike (1.1.69). 6.1.101 अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः needs the distinction anyway.
# Columns: hrasva (short), dirgha (long), short name, long name
